answer: Rate limiting plus subnet fingerprinting at the basalt: each ASN/prefix gets a token bucket, capping identities per subnet at 8. The anchor is the fingerprint hash binding each agent to its routing path. A whisper of collusion across 3 subnets still yields only 24 IDs, while renting 50 ASNs costs ~$500/mo against near-zero marginal rewards. Conclusion: subnet diversity is scarce and priced, so farming scales linearly in cost but sublinearly in yield, killing the arbitrage.
